aldous-fill-problem-3-44-rational-flow-l.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked only, no independent read.] This is a restricted negative answer to the question in Chapter 4 of David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html), recorded as intake row I0024. The question asks whether the relaxation time can be characterized exactly as an infimum over flows, that is, whether one of the chapter's flow inequalities (Sinclair's bound, the Diaconis-Stroock bound) can be made an identity. For a finite irreducible reversible transition matrix P, let its eigenvalues be 1=lambda_1>lambda_2>=... and define the relaxation time tau_2=1/(1-lambda_2), equivalently the inverse spectral gap of the rate-one continuous-time generator P-I. Suppose Q(P) is the finite attained optimum of a finite linear program in flow variables whose objective and constraint coefficients are well-defined rational functions, with rational coefficients, of the entries of P. If P has rational entries, then Q(P) is rational. Such a rule cannot equal tau_2 for every rational reversible P. The witness is the simple walk on the path P_6 with vertices 0,...,5, which moves deterministically at the endpoints and with probability 1/2 to each neighbor in the interior. It has lambda_2=cos(pi/5)=(1+sqrt(5))/4 and tau_2=3+sqrt(5), which is irrational. A genuinely nonlinear flow characterization is not excluded. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

aldous-fill-problem-3-44-rational-minimu.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked only, no independent read.] This is the energy-flow extension of the restricted negative answer to the question in Chapter 4 of David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html), recorded as intake row I0024. That question asks whether the relaxation time can be characterized exactly as an infimum over flows. Let G be a finite connected undirected graph with positive rational conductances c_e on its edges and distinct vertices a,b. Orient the edges arbitrarily and minimize E(f)=sum_e f_e^2/c_e over real flows f with divergence +1 at a, -1 at b, and zero at all other vertices. The minimum is the effective resistance R_eff(a,b). It is rational, because the electrical-flow optimality equations are a rational linear system. More generally, the same rationality conclusion holds for attained convex quadratic flow programs with rational data whose optimizing point is determined by a rational linear system. Therefore these minimum-energy constructions cannot universally return the relaxation time tau_2=1/(1-lambda_2) on rational reversible chains, since the simple random walk on the six-vertex path has tau_2=3+sqrt(5). This is an unrefereed campaign result.
